Subject: Residency evidence request: operational criteria for geo-pin and short-hop processing

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this. Our legal and security teams need a succinct set of operational artifacts to satisfy our internal compliance review for region residency. Specifically we need:

- Clear acceptance criteria that we (Acme Health) can use to verify that data-at-rest and inference compute are "pinned" to the EU region for our tenant.
- A short runbook that explains: when transient cross-region processing ("short hop" or ephemeral-egress) is permitted, the exact preconditions and approvals required, and how the event is logged and audited.
- The current subprocessor roster (names + jurisdictions) and whether any agents/processes might process content outside the EU during maintenance windows.
- An expected timeline for you to deliver the artifacts and any suggested point-of-contact for follow-up questions or a short technical call.

We aim to close this as part of our vendor assessment by 2026-11-25. Can you let me know whether you can provide the materials and a proposal for an operational acceptance test?

Regards,
Evelyn Turner
Data Protection Officer
Acme Health

Evelyn,

Appreciate the clear list — we can deliver the artifacts you outlined. Quick summary of what we'll provide and the controls we recommend for your acceptance test:

1) Residency acceptance criteria (summary):
   - Data storage and long-term logs for your tenant are provisioned in eu-west-1 (Ireland) by default and marked with a tenant-region tag.
   - Compute for inference is scheduled on capacity pools bound to eu-west-1. Failover to other regions only occurs under Exceptional Failover (see below) and requires two triggers: capacity alarm AND routing override with ticketed approval.
   - Short-hop / transient-egress: allowed strictly for maintenance/repairs and automated patching only when all of the following are true: customer-signed transient-egress clause executed; operations runbook pre-approved; ephemeral keys rotated post-event; event entry in immutable audit log. Default maximum transient window: 6 hours, configurable up to 72 hours with additional controls.

2) Runbook deliverable (we will attach):
   - Step-by-step detection->approval->execution->postmortem flow with checklist items, responsible roles, and required log evidence.

3) Subprocessor roster: the CSV will list subprocessors, regions, and whether they may perform any processing outside eu-west-1.

4) Acceptance test proposal:
   - We propose a scripted test that verifies: tenant resources pinned, simulated maintenance triggers a controlled ephemeral-egress under our lab account, and audit logs + KMS key rotation events are produced. Test duration: ~2 business days (prep + execution).

I will coordinate artifacts delivery by end-of-day Wednesday (2026-11-18). If you prefer an alignment call, can we do 30 minutes on Thursday 11/19? I will loop in our legal and ops leads.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
